trigger: The lecturer could not pass the electricity/depot comparisons or understand the evidence board, and described the teaching as disorganized and full of unexplained terms. The battery route was a clearer example.
diagnosis: Selecting a clue did not replace placed evidence until a second, poorly signposted placement action.
Evidence validation required a single canonical artifact even where newly authored artifacts supported the same conclusion.
Legacy experiments used hidden arbitrary thresholds instead of meaningful comparison conditions.
Reopening experiments did not render saved completion requirements until running another trial.
Area-level orientation did not provide plain-language foundational concepts throughout all five lessons.
XP levels had no functional advantages.
changes: Direct explanation/evidence selection, visible selected states, backward navigation and diagnostic feedback.
Explicitly authored alternative evidence with supporting explanations for the first two area puzzles; no automatic concept-overlap acceptance.
The preparatory electricity case now supplies both capacity and demand, enabling the selected case to support the deficit conclusion.
Visible comparison checklist, saved trial log, guided control presets and restored experiment interpretation.
Same-total feasible electricity comparisons and any distinct river-cost shares, with model interpretation still required.
32 plain-language learning goals and foundational concept sets; recommended route respects activity prerequisites.
Five XP levels unlock four usable assistance tools. Essential explanations are never XP-gated.
Previewing levels is isolated from learner saves.
scope: Original source course and all existing activities retained. Foundation guides organize and explain the source concepts; they do not certify empirical learning equivalence.
validation: test-learning-flow: supported alternate evidence, incorrect reasoning, restore invariants, comparison criteria, all presets, level thresholds and duplicate XP.
qa-puzzle-repair: direct replacement, backward navigation, saved answers, six experiments, 32 guides, working perks, admin isolation and mobile.
qa-module: complete authored activity and puzzle route, including incorrect-answer feedback without progression.
